rule: advisor F19 rule 101 - every --require string must have a demonstrated failing polarity on a real commit
method: Build a throwaway commit that ships the wrong default, then run the unmodified witness set against it. The throwaway sets Table.compiledDefault = .shipped and updates defaultRouteWitness to match, which is exactly the commit a careless change would produce, because defaultRouteWitnessNamesTheCompiledDefaults keeps the two in step.

control_commit.subject: THROWAWAY: ship the shipped table as the compiled default (Rule 101 polarity control)
control_commit.disposition: branch deleted after the proof; it is not an ancestor of the submitted tree

assertions_that_fired: FAIL require 'e120_default_route/tiered_switch/onepass67': found 0 copies, expected at least 1

reading: The route witness is a real discriminator. It reports 1 copy on the shipped tree and 0 copies on a tree whose only difference is the compiled-in table, and its paired forbid reports the complement. Every other assertion in the set held on both trees, so neither result comes from a broad build difference. Both polarities are therefore demonstrated on real commits, which is what rule 101 requires.
residual_limit: The witness proves which literal the binary carries. It cannot by itself prove that the literal names the constants the dispatcher reads, because a literal is not an expression over those constants. defaultRouteWitnessNamesTheCompiledDefaults closes that gap in the test suite, and the 512-token default leg closes it end to end by selecting tiered_switch with onepass67 and 7 QMV specializations with no environment set.
